Vivian (AE): Hey @Marcus, quick help needed — FinScale is asking for an annual commitment discount but they can only route payments as three invoices over the first year (Q1, Q2, Q3). Customer: FinScale, logo procurement constraints. Proposed: 2yr term, $240k ARR, standard annual-upfront 10% discount. They want to pay Year1 as 3x invoices (50%, 25%, 25%) instead of full upfront. Can Deal Desk approve exception or suggest alternatives?
Marcus (Deal Desk): looping in @Ana and @Priya. Do we have credit info + PO draft? What's the requested invoice schedule exactly?
Vivian (AE): PO draft coming from the customer — PO# FS-PO-0987. Schedule they requested: Year1 invoices on: 2026-04-01 (50%), 2026-07-01 (25%), 2026-10-01 (25%). Year2 they want annual prepay on 2027-04-01. They said accounting treats Year1 as ramped spend. They still want the 10% annual-upfront pricing applied to the 2yr commit if possible.
Ana (Finance): Got it. Need two things before we can greenlight non-standard terms: 1) credit review (we can do quick bureau check) 2) proposed invoice wording that commits the customer to the full 2yr spend (even if split invoices). If we accept split invoices we shift DSO risk. What’s their billing contact and legal entity name?
Vivian (AE): Billing contact is ops@finscale.com, legal entity FinScale, Inc. I can attach a short commitment clause in the SOW. Customer already sent a PDF PO with signature.
Priya (Legal): I can draft a payment schedule addendum. Two legal asks: must include an explicit non-cancellation clause for the committed term and a clause that any missed invoice triggers immediate acceleration of remaining committed amount. Also need defined invoice dispute window (30 days).
Tom (Solutions): Quick note — we validated model sizing for FinScale load. If we accept split invoices we should avoid granting the quant/usage incentives until Year1 is fully collected; otherwise cost exposures stack up.
Marcus (Deal Desk): From pricing perspective: annual-upfront 10% discount is tied to full Year1 prepay. If we allow split invoices but require they are all due in Year1 and define acceleration on default, we could treat as equivalent for discount. Alternative is 5% partial-prepay discount now + standard pricing on remaining. Which does AE prefer?
Vivian (AE): Customer strongly prefers the 10% — they argued procurement needs invoices quarterly to match budget lines. I can push for bank guarantee but they prefer PO. If Legal and Finance can accept the acceleration clause + credit check, we can keep 10%.
Ana (Finance): Running a soft credit check now. If risk is medium-high we should require either: a) 50% upfront today + split for the rest, or b) an approved credit term (Net30) for the split invoices plus landmark PO that references the 2yr commitment. If credit passes, finance ok to accept the split with the acceleration clause and invoice schedule.
Marcus (Deal Desk): Decision path for deal desk: approve 10% annual-upfront discount if all three conditions met: 1) credit check passes, 2) PO references full 2yr commitment and discount, 3) Legal addendum with acceleration on missed invoice. If any fail, fallback to 5% discount with 50% upfront. Approving on those terms. @DealDeskBot please record provisional approval.
DealDeskBot: Recorded provisional approval for FIN-0987: 10% annual-upfront discount contingent on credit pass + PO clause + legal addendum. Reference ID: DD-1832-01.
Vivian (AE): Thanks — I'll send PO to legal and copy finance. Quick question: can we include an invoice sample line in the SOW so procurement is happy? Something like:
```
Invoice 1 (50%): $120,000 — due 2026-04-01
Invoice 2 (25%): $60,000 — due 2026-07-01
Invoice 3 (25%): $60,000 — due 2026-10-01
All invoices reference Purchase Order FS-PO-0987 and this SOW which commits to a two-year term at $240,000 ARR with annual-upfront pricing (10% discount) applied to Year1 on receipt of invoices as scheduled.
```
Marcus (Deal Desk): That wording looks fine to me. Ensure the clause: "Failure to pay any installment when due will result in immediate acceleration of unpaid total commitment amount."
Priya (Legal): Agreed. I'll add acceleration + 30-day cure period language and a specific reference to invoice numbers and PO. I'll also add a sentence clarifying that the discount applies only if all Year1 invoices are paid per schedule.
Ana (Finance): Credit check returned CONCERN: some late payments flagged historically but no bankruptcies. Risk score medium. We still can accept conditional approval but require Customer Operations to set Net30 on split invoices and require collections holdback: disable certain credit-based features until Invoice2 is paid. Can Sales accept that operational constraint?
Vivian (AE): I can live with a collections holdback on advanced features as long as we keep 10% discount. Customer is okay with Net30 and understands holdback. They want to close this week.
Marcus (Deal Desk): Final: Deal Desk approves 10% annual-upfront pricing contingent on: completed credit check (we have medium risk but acceptable), signed PO referencing FS-PO-0987 and 2yr commitment, Legal addendum with acceleration + 30-day cure + discount-clause, Finance to set Net30 and implement collections holdback until Invoice2 clears. I'll mark approval as final and attach DD-1832-APPROVED.
DealDeskBot: Approval finalized: DD-1832-APPROVED. Next steps: @Vivian upload signed PO + attach legal addendum link.
Vivian (AE): Uploaded PO and pinged customer for signed addendum. Thanks everyone :tada:
Tom (Solutions): Noted operational holdback — we'll gate the advanced KV-caching feature until Invoice2 payment clears. I'll add a short runbook for Ops.
Priya (Legal): I'll send the finalized addendum to all for signature in ~30m.
Ana (Finance): I'll create the invoice schedule in billing portal when addendum is signed and set Net30.
Vivian (AE): Great — closing now. Will follow up if anything changes. :v:
